hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 1]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 2]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

In other words, the line of reflection is the perpendicular bisector between any pair of corresponding points in the image and the pre-image.

options.definition: The figure *after* one or more transformations

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
Since the $x$-axis is *horizontal*, the reflection will move each point of $\triangle ABC$ *vertically* across the axis.

For example, point $B$ is $5$ units above the $x$-axis, so $B'$ will be $5$ units below the axis.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C with point A at negative two, zero, point B at negative six, five, and point C at negative four, four. A dashed arrow points at both point B prime at negative six, negative five and point B.

hints.content:
We can reflect each of the other vertices in the same way.


[[☃ image 1]]

We note that points $A$ and $A'$ are in the same place because $A$ was on the line of reflection.

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C with point A at negative two, zero, point B at negative six, five, and point C at negative four, four. A dashed arrow points at both point B prime at negative six, negative five and point B. A dashed arrow points at both point C prime at negative four, negative four and point C. Point A prime is at the same point as point A.
